data.long_meaning: From the Greek name Kandaxos, derived from kandēs meaning 'pure, innocent'. In Greek mythology, the name was borne by a man who was a friend of Perseus and helped him defeat the Gorgon Medusa. The name Kandace carries the meaning “Pure, innocent” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kandace usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, innocent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Candace
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Candace originates from the Greek Κανδακη, meaning aeternal joy or radiant joy. In the Early Christian Church, Candace was notably the name of the Queen of Ethiopia mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles.

in_english.name: Kandace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kandace is derived from the Greek Κανδακη (Kandake), which signifies eternal joy or radiant happiness. It is rooted in Christian tradition through its appearance in the New Testament, specifically in the Acts of the Apostles (8:27), referring to the Queen of Ethiopia. Historically, the name has been associated with nobility and spiritual significance. In modern Christian cultures, Kandace symbolizes a person of joy, faith, and strength.
